Note API Reference¶

Back to PlussQit API Reference

This page documents pluss::Note and pluss::coden::Note in the same handwritten, usage-first style as the rest of the PlussQit object references: one method page at a time, with compiled-and-run examples under each method page rather than generated stubs.

The examples are intentionally written as standalone snippets: each example defines its own input object, stores intermediate results in named variables, and explicitly prints the result it is discussing. That makes the pages more reliable as copy-paste starting points and as templates for future Note documentation passes.

What Note Is¶

Note is the text payload object in PlussQit.

Use it when your data are strings, tokens, lines, snippets, prompts, LaTeX, or document fragments and you want to transform them in a shape-preserving, vectorized way.

That is the main difference from the other foundational objects:

  • Series carries numeric and boolean values.

  • Note carries UTF-8 text or raw byte-oriented textual content.

  • Timeline carries temporal values.

  • TimeIndex is the ordered 1D time-axis surface built for lookup, slicing, and alignment.

Includes¶

#include <pluss/pluss.h>
// or the narrower surface
#include <pluss/coden/coden.h>
#include <pluss/coden/note_factory.h>

Practical Construction Patterns¶

Example 1. Build a scalar text value.

auto title = pluss::make_note("Final Exam Review");

Example 2. Build a 1D batch of text cases.

auto names = pluss::make_note({"Ada Lovelace", "Grace Hopper", "Linus"});

Example 3. Build from flat storage plus explicit shape when the text already arrives from another system in flattened form.

std::vector<std::string> flat{"r0c0", "r0c1", "r1c0", "r1c1"};
std::array<std::int64_t, 2> sizes{2, 2};

auto grid = pluss::make_note(flat, sizes);

How to Read the Examples¶

Most Note methods preserve shape and operate cell by cell.

That means when you see a 1D Note with three cases, the transformed result is usually still a 1D Note with three cases. Tokenizing methods are the main exception: they return a TokenBatch, which flattens tokens into one Note plus an offsets() vector describing where each original case begins and ends inside that flattened token stream.

Using This Reference¶

  • Use the left sidebar to open one Note method page at a time.

  • This first handwritten slice focuses on the methods users reach for early: cleanup, substring matching, replacement, tokenization, regex extraction, NLP-adjacent cleanup, and TeX escaping.

  • Every method page below embeds its output directly under the example that produced it.

  • Those outputs were verified against the current library state from the examples/CodeN/note_docverify_demo.cpp run, but the page itself stays self-contained instead of delegating readers into one large verifier dump.

Coverage¶

This first Note pass now covers:

  • substring predicates: contains

  • byte-length inspection: lengths_bytes

  • case normalization: lower

  • URL cleanup for text preprocessing: nlp_remove_urls

  • regex token extraction: regex_findall

  • elementwise substring replacement: replace

  • literal substring removal: remove_all

  • boundary quoting: quote

  • delimiter-based and whitespace-based tokenization: split, split_lines, split_whitespace, tokenize_words

  • line and whitespace tokenization: split_lines, split_whitespace

  • boundary trimming: strip

  • targeted text masking: nlp_mask_pii, nlp_remove_urls

  • TeX-safe escaping and TeX-to-text reduction: tex_escape, tex_to_text

  • transport encodings: base64_encode, url_encode

The rest of the Note surface is much larger than this first slice. It includes broader cleanup families, NLP helpers, TeX parsers, token comparison helpers, and encoding transforms. Those will be expanded method by method in later passes rather than bulk-filled with shallow prose.
